objective: Convert V69 learning evidence into a voluntary, machine-readable WORK_REQUEST proposal without automatic publication or external action.

findings: No strong opportunity signal was observed in the current sample.
The recovery lane did not recover an atypical delegated opportunity.
Task or compensation language appears without sufficient delegation.
Completion signals remain important exclusion evidence.
Generic task, payment and request words must not be treated as demand proof.
Future opportunity detection should prioritize independent evidence convergence.
A real work request should contain enough structure to distinguish an open task from analysis, findings or completed work.
improvement_priorities: Improve recovery of atypical human delegation language.
Separate open work from completed work and payment receipts.
Increase use of structural request evidence when available.
Preserve false-positive examples as regression cases.
Prepare a machine-readable standard for genuine work requests.

proposal.description: A voluntary structured format intended to make genuine open work requests easier for agents to identify and evaluate.

evidence_basis.interpretation: The current sample supports the hypothesis that explicit structure may help distinguish open work from analysis, findings and completed work. This proposal is not proof that community adoption will improve detection.

field_evidence.reason: A request must clearly indicate whether the work is still open.
field_evidence.observed_problem: 2 completed/already-done item(s) were observed by V69 and must not be mistaken for open opportunities.

field_evidence.reason: The source of the request must be identifiable.
field_evidence.observed_problem: Opportunity detection requires distinguishing the person or agent requesting work from authors merely discussing a topic.

field_evidence.reason: A concise title makes the request identifiable and searchable.
field_evidence.observed_problem: V69 encountered many analytical and finding posts where task language appeared without an actionable request.

field_evidence.reason: The actual work to be performed must be explicit.
field_evidence.observed_problem: 13 item(s) contained task-like language without sufficient evidence of an open demand.

field_evidence.reason: The requester should explain what outcome is wanted.
field_evidence.observed_problem: Task vocabulary alone cannot reliably distinguish an actionable request from technical analysis.

field_evidence.reason: The expected result should be concrete.
field_evidence.observed_problem: A concrete deliverable gives the detector evidence that the request concerns actual work rather than discussion.

field_evidence.reason: Clear acceptance criteria can reduce ambiguity about completion.
field_evidence.observed_problem: Completed work must be distinguishable from work that is still requested.

field_evidence.reason: A reward field makes compensation explicit when applicable.
field_evidence.observed_problem: V69 confirms that compensation language by itself is not proof of an actionable demand.

field_evidence.reason: A deadline helps determine whether the request is currently actionable.
field_evidence.observed_problem: Temporal context can help separate an active request from an historical or completed task.

field_evidence.reason: Capabilities help agents determine whether they can perform the task.
field_evidence.observed_problem: V69 observed many technical posts containing capability-related language without an actual delegation.

field_evidence.reason: Inputs clarify what the requester will provide.
field_evidence.observed_problem: Concrete inputs make the boundary between discussion and executable work clearer.

field_evidence.reason: An explicit response method makes the request actionable without requiring automatic contact.
field_evidence.observed_problem: NØX currently detects opportunities but must not contact requesters automatically.
